sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **First Session (1885, Bombay)**: Presided over by **W.C. Bonnerjee**; attended by 72 delegates; foundational birthplace at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College.
• **First Muslim President (1887, Madras)**: **Badruddin Tyabji** presided over the 3rd session, emphasizing pan-Indian Muslim participation.
• **First British President (1888, Allahabad)**: **George Yule** presided, proving the INC's open, non-sectarian character.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The rotating presidency rule ensured that the President of the session was chosen from a region other than the province where the session was held.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Rotation Principle**: INC sessions were held across different provincial capitals (Bombay, Calcutta, Madras, Allahabad, Lahore, Faizpur) to foster national integration.
• **Driving Advantages**: Showcasing local nationalist leadership, mobilizing regional masses, and preventing British branding of the INC as a regional body.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Regional friction over venue selection, caste/religion representation debates, and ideological rifts.
• **Policy Interventions**: Adoption of compromises, inclusion of socio-economic resolutions, and institutionalization of working committees.

items.title: Mnemonic for First Four INC Sessions
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **B**ombay, **M**adras, **A**llahabad, **B**ombay (BMAB) -> Presidents: **B**onnerjee, **T**yabji, **Y**ule, **W**edderburn (BTYW).
• **Decoded Meaning**: 1885 (Bombay-Bonnerjee), 1886 (Calcutta-Naoroji excluded in short mnemonic, focus on 85-88), 1887 (Madras-Tyabji), 1888 (Allahabad-Yule), 1889 (Bombay-Wedderburn).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly matches early sessions, presidents, and locations without confusion.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember landmark milestones via 3 'S's: **1905** (Swadeshi start), **1906** (Swaraj Calcutta), **1907** (Surat Split).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently tricks aspirants by stating that 'Swaraj' was first defined as complete independence (Purna Swaraj) in 1906. Clarification: In 1906, Swaraj meant self-government under British paramountcy; Purna Swaraj was adopted much later in Lahore (1929).

Mains Value Addition: Analyze the Lucknow Session (1916) not just as a merger, but critically examine the 'separate electorates' concession to the Muslim League as the genesis of communal electoral politics.

keyTakeaways: The early INC sessions successfully built an all-India political platform through rotating regional presidencies.
Ideological shifts at Calcutta (1906) and Surat (1907) transformed the character of the national movement from petitioning to mass agitation.
The Lucknow Session (1916) marked the temporary zenith of Hindu-Muslim political cooperation and nationalist consolidation.
